text: As the Patriots prepare to host the Steelers for their 2026 home opener at Gillette Stadium on Sunday, September 20 at 1 PM ET, the team faces a significant challenge with wide receiver A.J. Brown headed to injured reserve after suffering a high ankle sprain in Week 1, sidelining him for at least four games—a blow that will require contributions from other receivers stepping into larger roles in the offense. On the roster front, the Patriots re-signed safety Elliott Davison to the practice squad while releasing tight end Shane Zylstra from the practice squad, minor adjustments as the team prepares for Pittsburgh. Beyond football matters, the week has showcased the Patriots organization's commitment to community engagement: Drake Maye and his wife Ann Michael funded classroom wish lists for more than 50 teachers and support staff at Alfred Lima Sr. Elementary School in Providence, while the Kraft family and Patriots Foundation donated $275,000 through the Myra Kraft Community MVP Award program, recognizing twenty-six volunteers including Susie Shaw of Carlisle, MA, who received the $25,000 grand prize for William's Be Yourself Challenge—efforts that underscore the franchise's values as quarterback Maye and company look to bounce back against Pittsburgh.
